description: A binary `-` with a literal zero minuend (RFC §5.4.7). `0 - x` and `-x` differ when x is +0.0 (`0 - 0.0` is +0.0, `-(0.0)` is -0.0), so `-(0, x)` collapses ONLY when x is a numeric literal, and then folds to the exact difference `0 - x`. With a non-literal subtrahend the binary node is kept, minuend and all. A double unary negation still collapses, which is exact. `max` only carries the cases: it is structure-preserving. The float-zero literal cases (`-(0, 0.0)`, `-(0.0, -0.0)` and `-(0.0, 5)`, giving 0.0, 0.0 and -5.0) are pinned in each binding's own canonicalize tests instead: a wire reader may read an integral float token such as `0.0` as an integer (CONFORMANCE_SPEC §5.5.3 rule 3), so they cannot be written portably here.
